get.summary: List published versions for a package by PURL
get.description:
Given a package URL (PURL) *without* a version, returns every version
Socket knows about for that package along with its publish date, sorted
newest-first by publish date.

This lets you enforce version policies such as "N-1" (allow the previous
release, block the newest) without querying a package registry directly.
Versions with no known publish date are listed last.

**Ordering includes prereleases.** Sorting is by publish date only, so
index 0 is the most recently *published* version, not necessarily the
newest stable release. On npm in particular the newest publishes are
often canaries or release candidates, so a consumer that reads index 1
as "N-1" can land on a prerelease. Each entry carries a `prerelease`
flag for this: filter out entries where `prerelease` is `true` before
applying an N-1 rule. `prerelease` is `null` when the ecosystem's
version grammar has no canonical prerelease parser, or when the version
string itself does not parse — treat null according to your own policy
rather than as an error.

Pass `limit` to cap how many entries come back; it is applied after
sorting, so `limit=2` is all the N-1 use case needs. A `limit` that
is not a positive integer is rejected with a 400 rather than clamped.

The PURL must be percent-encoded as a single path segment
(`encodeURIComponent`); an unencoded `/` will not match this route.
Any version on the PURL is ignored — the full history always comes back.
The HuggingFace `type` qualifier (model, dataset, or space) is honored.

A well-formed PURL for an ecosystem that does not support version
listing returns a 400 rather than a server error.

Authentication: Organization API token, OAuth2, or NextAuth session.
Required token scope: `packages:list`. Costs 100 quota units.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of version entries to return, applied after sorting. Omit for the full history.

parameters.name: purl
parameters.description: Package URL, percent-encoded as a single path segment. Example: pkg%3Anpm%2F%40babel%2Fcore

purl.description: The PURL as received, echoed back.

versions.description: Known versions, newest-first by publish date. Ordering includes prereleases, so index 0 is the most recent publish rather than the newest stable release.

version.description: The version string as the ecosystem reports it.

publishedAt.description: ISO-8601 publish date, or null when the ecosystem reports none. Undated versions are listed last.

prerelease.description: True when this version is a prerelease (canary, release candidate, dev, beta) according to the ecosystem's own version grammar. Null means unknown — either the ecosystem has no canonical prerelease parser, or this version string does not parse. Null is not an error.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of supply chain attack campaigns. Supports filtering
by status, ecosystem, and an incremental sync parameter (`updated_after`).

Package PURLs are not inlined on the campaign object — they are their own
paginated resource. Fetch them per campaign from
`/threat-campaigns/:campaign_id/packages`.

Authentication: Organization API token, OAuth2, or NextAuth session.
Required token scope: `threat-campaigns:list`.

This endpoint requires an Enterprise Plan with the Threat Feed add-on.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by campaign status. Defaults to ongoing.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: Filter by ecosystem (e.g. npm, pypi, maven).

parameters.name: updated_after
parameters.description: Unix timestamp in seconds. Only return campaigns updated after this time. Omit to return all matching campaigns.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of campaigns per page. Default 30, max 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Use the endCursor value from the previous response.

linkedThreatCount.description: Number of threat feed entries linked to this campaign.

linkedPackageArtifactsCount.description: Number of distinct package artifacts linked to this campaign.

htmlUrl.description: URL of the public campaign page on socket.dev, or null if the campaign has no public page.

get.description:
Returns a single supply chain attack campaign by ID. Same shape as one item
from the campaigns list; package PURLs are not inlined — fetch them from the
paginated `/threat-campaigns/:campaign_id/packages` resource instead.

Useful for filling in cached campaign metadata client-side when crawling the
campaigns list or packages feed.

Authentication: Organization API token, OAuth2, or NextAuth session.
Required token scope: `threat-campaigns:list`.

This endpoint requires an Enterprise Plan with the Threat Feed add-on.

linkedThreatCount.description: Number of threat feed entries linked to this campaign.

linkedPackageArtifactsCount.description: Number of distinct package artifacts linked to this campaign.

htmlUrl.description: URL of the public campaign page on socket.dev, or null if the campaign has no public page.

get.summary: List packages for a threat campaign
get.description:
Returns a cursor-paginated list of package PURLs affected by a single supply
chain attack campaign. This is the primary way to retrieve all packages for a
known campaign without an inline, unbounded list on the campaign object.

Pagination follows the same `{ items, endCursor }` envelope as the campaigns
list. Pass the `endCursor` value back as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

Authentication: Organization API token, OAuth2, or NextAuth session.
Required token scope: `threat-campaigns:list`.

This endpoint requires an Enterprise Plan with the Threat Feed add-on.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of packages per page. Default 100, max 1000.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Use the endCursor value from the previous response.

items.description: Package PURLs associated with this campaign.

post.summary: Check public npm packages for known malware
post.description: Returns bounded public malware observations for exact npm releases. Results are for this request only and are not cached.
